Recovery paths

`VaultWithdraw` and `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` call `canTransfer` between two pseudo-accounts (neither of which is the asset issuer), so the existing issuer carveout did not apply and withdrawals would fail with `tecNO_AUTH` after the issuer cleared `lsfMPTCanTransfer`.

A new `WaiveMPTCanTransfer` enum is threaded through `canTransfer`'s MPT and `Asset` overloads (default `No`, preserving every other call site). `VaultWithdraw` and `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` pass `Yes`, gated on the amendment.
Other transferability checks (IOU NoRipple, freeze, requireAuth) still apply.\r\n\r\n#### 2.

Vault share inheritance via `sfReferenceHolding`\r\n\r\nA new optional `UINT256` field on `MPTokenIssuance` points to the vault pseudo-account's holding for the underlying: the `MPToken` keylet for an MPT-backed vault, or the `RippleState` keylet for an IOU-backed vault.

XRP-backed vaults leave the field unset.

- `VaultCreate` populates the field at share-issuance creation. `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` validates the pointed-to SLE exists and is of an expected type (`ltMPTOKEN` or `ltRIPPLE_STATE`).
- `canTransfer(MPTIssue, ...)`, `canTrade(Asset)`, `isVaultPseudoAccountFrozen`, and `checkMPTAllowed` (AMM / Offer-crossing / Check) read `sfReferenceHolding`, fetch the holding SLE via `keylet::unchecked`, derive the underlying via a new `assetOfHolding` helper, and dispatch the same check recursively.
- Recursion is bounded at `kMAX_ASSET_CHECK_DEPTH` (vault-of-vault-shares is already forbidden at `VaultCreate`; the cap is defensive).

The bound and bookkeeping live inside the amendment-gated branch and are dead code pre-amendment.\r\n- The recovery-path waive short-circuits inheritance: callers operate on the vault's direct underlying, never on a share, so skipping the branch honors the recovery intent without transitively unlocking a deeper underlying.
The recursive call always passes `WaiveMPTCanTransfer::No`.\r\n\r\n#### 3.

Invariant

`ValidMPTIssuance` enforces, post-`fixCleanup3_2_0`:

- `sfReferenceHolding` may only be set on creation, only by `VaultCreate`.
- `sfReferenceHolding` is immutable on an existing `MPTokenIssuance`.
- Any `MPToken` / `RippleState` whose owner is a vault pseudo-account (account SLE has `sfVaultID`) may only be deleted by `VaultDelete`.

`visitEntry` bookkeeping is itself amendment-gated via the thread-local `isFeatureEnabled(fixCleanup3_2_0)` so pre-amendment transactions skip the new work entirely.

### API Impact

- [x] `libxrpl` change — new `sfReferenceHolding` field on `MPTokenIssuance`; new `WaiveMPTCanTransfer` enum; new `assetOfHolding` helper.

No public API or peer-protocol changes.

All behavior gated under `fixCleanup3_2_0`.

## Test Plan

Covered in `Vault_test`, `Loan_test`, and `Invariants_test`:

- `sfReferenceHolding` writer correctness — populated by `VaultCreate` for MPT/IOU underlyings, unset for XRP, absent pre-amendment, absent for plain `MPTokenIssuanceCreate`.
- Recovery paths — post-amendment `VaultWithdraw` / `LoanBrokerCoverWithdraw` succeed after issuer clears `lsfMPTCanTransfer`; pre-amendment regression confirms historical failure mode.
- Share inheritance — P2P share Payment and IOU `NoRipple` propagation through `canTransfer`; DEX offers blocked through `canTrade`; AMM creation with shares blocked through `checkMPTAllowed` when the underlying `CanTrade` is cleared.
- Holding-deletion probes — full-balance `Clawback`, iss …

This means `AMMClawback` cannot override individual or deep freeze on AMM trust lines (between the AMM pseudo-account and the issuer).

The `withdraw()` call succeeds because it uses `FreezeHandling::fhIGNORE_FREEZE`, but the invariant checker then rejects the transaction because it detects a balance change on a frozen AMM line without the override condition being met.

This creates a contradiction where the issuer's freeze action prevents their own clawback from the AMM pool.\r\n\r\nWhen the issuer individually freezes their AMM trust line (via TrustSet targeting the AMM pseudo-account with `tfSetFreeze`), all subsequent AMMClawback transactions against any holder in that pool will fail at the invariant check.

Combined with the fact that a frozen holder cannot withdraw via regular AMMWithdraw, this creates a freeze/clawback deadlock where LP tokens are effectively locked until the issuer unfreezes the AMM line.

### Context of Change
Change from:
```if ((!isAMMLine || globalFreeze) && hasPrivilege(tx, overrideFreeze))```
to:
```if (hasPrivilege(tx, overrideFreeze))```
The overrideFreeze privilege is already restricted to AMMClawback transactions only (via transactions.macro), so removing the AMM line check is safe.

Generalized several of the amount-related helper classes to understand `Asset`s.

___________________________________________________________________________
Some refactor happens because I want to call some functions from AMMWithdraw.
**1.

Refactor of `withdraw`:**
- Added static `withdraw` function to return the `amountWithdrawActual` and `amount2WithdrawActual` as well.
- private overload `withdraw`.
- Previously in `withdraw` function, it checks `if (!(ctx_.tx[sfFlags] & (tfWithdrawAll | tfOneAssetWithdrawAll)))` to decide if it needs to call `adjustAmountsByLPTokens`.
Because these flags only belong to `AMMWithdraw`, to make this function also work for AMMClawback, I changed it by passing enum WithdrawAll.\r\n\r\n**2.
Refactor of `equalWithdrawTokens`:**\r\n Because I want to call this function in `AMMClawback`, I make a public static `equalWithdrawTokens` function.
And also private overload `equalWithdrawTokens`\r\n\r\n**3.

Added `deleteAMMAccountIfEmpty`**
 Since I need to reuse the logic in AMMWithdraw that when all the tokens are withdrawn, the amm account is deleted, so I added function `deleteAMMAccountIfEmpty`.

___________________________________________________________________________
**Reason of adding flag `tfClawTwoAssets`:**
If the issuer issues both assets `A` and `B` in the amm pool, when clawing back `A`, `tfClawTwoAssets` is used to decide if the paired token `B` to be clawed back as well or goes back to the holder.
If tfClawTwoAssets` is set true, the paired token will be clawed back as well.

Otherwise, the paired token goes back to the holder.

**Reason of adding both `asset` and `amount` in the `AMMClawback` request:**
`amount` is used to decide if the issuer wants to clawback all the tokens or not.

(if `amount` is not provided, then clawback all) Imagine if an issuer issues both asset `A` and `B` in the amm pool, and the issuer wants to clawback all `A` and give back all the corresponding `B` to the holder.

Then the issuer just needs to specify `A` in `asset` field and leave out `amount` field.

**Reasons for setting tfee as 0:**
Because we are doing a two-asset withdrawal. tfee is not used.

**Reasons for using asset1 and asset2 to navigate amm**
To keep the same with other amm transactions and make it simple.
So we require providing asset1 and asset2 in the AMMClawback request.
